idiom_name: accessor (get) with a cached promise (self-memoizing getter)
implementation_notes: The getter is the holder: JavaScript accessors compute on read and the caching is written by hand (MDN notes getters are not lazy by themselves), so the idiom is a self-memoizing getter that stores the first result - for a store read, usually a promise: 'get author() { return (this.#authorPromise ??= gateway.find(this.authorId)); }'. The first read starts the query and stores the promise, later reads reuse it, and concurrent readers share the same in-flight promise; Object.defineProperty accessors do the same on plain objects, and a Proxy get trap covers names only known at runtime. A getter cannot await, so asynchronous stores are exposed as the promise (or an explicit load() method) and callers await it.
pitfalls: A rejected promise is cached by ??= / ||=: the failure sticks until the field is cleared, so choose retry versus cache deliberately and always provide the reset path.
Every accessor becomes an I/O trigger, so loops over objects produce N+1 queries; and JSON.stringify skips getters (they are not enumerable own properties), silently omitting the deferred value.
Getters are synchronous: a lazy load must be represented as a promise or an explicit method, because code that needs the value synchronously sees a pending promise, not data.
